title: 2027 IEEE Symposium on CI in Security, Defence and Biometrics (IEEE CISDB)
summary: IEEE CISDB focuses on computational intelligence in security, defence, and biometrics.

sections.heading: Symposium Chairs
bullets: Prof. Jiankun Hu - jiankun.hu@unsw.edu.au, The University of New South Wales, IEEE Member
Tianqing Zhu - tqzhu@cityu.edu.mo, City University of Macau

sections.heading: Scope
paragraphs: Cyberattacks have come a long way since the first worm, CREEPER, was released on the ARPANET followed by the first defence, REAPER. In recent years, Ubiquitous cyberattacks have become more sophisticated with advanced persistent threats (APT), polymorphic viruses, ransomware, phishing schemes, zero-day attacks and other sinister worms. Enterprises are always playing catch-up. Meanwhile, governments across the world have woken up to critical re-thinking of what the cyber world is from a perspective of not only its usefulness but also the threats and limitations it brings. A host of security directives, regulations, and strategies have been created to enhance data and critical infrastructure protection mechanisms to not only become secure and resilient but also improve privacy and trust.

This symposium aims to provide a comprehensive exploration of Computational Intelligence (CI) models and applications in the realms of security and resilience. Delving into the past, present, and future, the symposium will address challenges, advancements, and emerging trends to foster collaboration among researchers, practitioners, and industry experts.

We are seeking contributions that address either theoretical developments or practical applications in this field. Further, the symposium aims to promote collaboration and the sharing of knowledge to develop the field of CI in Security, Defence and Biometrics.

sections.heading: Topics of Interest
paragraphs: Topics of interest include, but are not limited to:

sections.heading: Cyber Security
bullets: Securing sensor, wireless, cellular, broadband and 5G/6G networks
Sensor fusion and decision support for mobile device security
Identification and prevention of zero-day exploits

sections.heading: Defence
bullets: Modelling adversarial behaviour for threat detection
Modelling adversarial behaviour for situation and impact assessment
Process and user refinement for defence operations

sections.heading: Biometrics and identity management
bullets: Soft biometrics and new biometric modalities
Mobile biometric devices and embedded systems
